content:
(Inspired by #41845)
Sometimes PRs cause slowdowns unexpectantly and is only noticed after the PR is merged, by landing in #rss > Significant commits to mathlib4 .

Since most people probably don't look at the channel, I wonder if it would be worth it (and doable) for a bot to write a comment on GitHub on the PR a comment as a warning after the (merged) PR has landed in #rss > Significant commits to mathlib4.

This would notify the authors of the PR that caused slowdowns more easily.

seems like a worthwhile feature for the radar bot?
cc: @Joscha Mennicken

Felix Pernegger said:

most people probably don't look at the channel

Is this true?

This would work for those who don't look at the channel but do look at their GH notifications. You could go further and @ them on Zulip.
I used to have the #rss muted since there was a lot of stuff, but now I do look at it
I don't look at #rss but I do look at GH notifications.

The relevant Zulip topic is #rss > Significant commits to mathlib4, isn't it?

I for myself completely muted all notifications from mathlib4 on github because relevant notifications from other repos got drowned by them and afaik github doesn't provide a way to still get notified about direct mentions without also getting updates about any PR you participated in. So this would just go onto the pile of spam.

I personally would appreciate a @ in that rss topic though. That should reach you even when the topic is muted (not though when not subscribed to the channel at all) and zulip has great options to customise notifications. Might only work for people who have their github user in their zulip profile.
